title: At Risk table lists customers by 12-month revenue, highest first
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
  2. You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  3. You are in a location (workplace) with several at-risk customers (use the window that gives the most rows, e.g. 30 days).

Setup

  • For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on.
  • For 3: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: the At Risk Customers tile shows 2 or more on at least one window. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data.
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu, set the At Risk window and read the headline.
  2. Click View details on At Risk Customers.
  3. Read the Revenue (12 Mo) column from top to bottom, on every page.
  4. Look for two customers with the same Revenue (12 Mo) and check their order by name.
  5. Count the rows in the table (all pages).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The table is ordered by Revenue (12 Mo), highest first (e.g. $1,209.50 above $40.50).
  • Customers with the same amount are listed by name, A to Z.
  • The number of rows equals the headline: every at-risk customer is listed and none is silently left out.
  • If a workplace ever has more than 500 at-risk customers, the table shows the first 500 in that order and says "Showing 500 of N at-risk customers", while the headline still counts all N. This cannot be reached by hand on normal data; write 'cap not reached' in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9578 (Story 6, Expanding a Tile); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 6. Design canvas board 09_AtRisk_After (row 9) for the table columns.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S6-R8: “The At Risk Customers tile expands to the At Risk Customers table. The table is ordered by each customer's trailing-twelve-month revenue, highest first, with the customer name as the tiebreaker, so the largest amount at risk reads first. The table lists every at-risk customer. A safety cap of 500 rows applies: if a workplace ever exceeds it, the table shows the first 500 in that order and says so on screen, reading "Showing 500 of N at-risk customers", while the headline still counts every one. The table never truncates silently, because a table that stops short while the headline counts more is a defect: the two then disagree.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
